brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A green tea from Yantai in Shandong, a national geographical indication made in flat, curled and needle shapes.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It is counted among Shandong's ten famous teas. Little is documented about how it developed.
processing: Typical of green tea: picked, heated soon after picking to stop oxidation, then shaped and dried.
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Flat tea is straight, smooth and emerald; curled tea is tight and grey-green with a frosty bloom; needle tea is fine, round, straight and green.
appearance_wet: Even and tender, thick in the curled style and plump in the needle style.
taste_profile: Flat tea has a lasting aroma and a mellow body; curled tea is rich with a sweet return; needle tea is clean and gentle.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
